title: O May My Soul, Uncrushed by Care
description: O May My Soul, Uncrushed by Care in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns of the Greek Church (Edinburgh and London, 1900).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O may my soul, un-crushed by care, Di-rect her gaze to where Thou art, And in Thy splen-dour find, O Christ, The strength of life Thou canst im-part.

lines: O may my soul, uncrushed by care,
Direct her gaze to where Thou art,
And in Thy splendour find, O Christ,
The strength of life Thou canst impart.
And freed from sin's depressing load,
May I pursue the path divine,
And rise above the cares of earth
Until my life is merged in Thine.
Who tunes his harp to sound Thy praise,
And still my life shall hymn Thy love,
And glory to the Father raise.
And when I rest in glory bright,
The burden of my labour past,
In hymns I'll praise Thee more and more

source: John Brownlie, Hymns of the Greek Church (1900)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns of the Greek Church; set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
